lines.directed: Textual note: The ten Sanskrit sūtras are attested in the standard 77-sūtra recension. The explanatory reading follows Kṣemarāja’s Śivasūtravimarśinī, especially his distinctions concerning mantra, limited siddhis, Khecarī, Mātṛkā and the subsidence of pure knowledge. Traditional supernatural and cosmological claims have been presented as the tradition’s claims, not verified physical phenomena. The humorous narration is original rather than a quotation of Kṣemarāja.
Next comes the longest and most extraordinary part of the text.

The limited individual, the return of bondage, the construction of experience, the role of the senses, the breath, embodiment, liberation in daily life, and one of the most beautiful sequences in all Kashmir Śaivism:
